newsitem.title: FRANCE: MOTOR RACING-UNHAPPY SUNRISE FOR WOLLEK.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-UNHAPPY SUNRISE FOR WOLLEK.

text.p: The works Porsche driven by Frenchman Bob Wollek that had led a good part of the way crashed out of the Le Mans 24 Hours endurance classic on Sunday.
The Porsche 911 which Wollek was driving with German Hans Stuck and Thierry Boutsen of Belgium spun off at the Arnage bend with two thirds of the race run. He was unhurt.
Another factory Porsche driven by Frenchman Yannick Dalmas, with Ralf Kelleners of Germany and compatriot Emmanuel Collard, took the lead.

They were one lap ahead of the Porsche TWR prototype of the Joest stable, winners in 1996, driven by exFormula One racers Michele Alboreto of Italy and Stefan Johansson of Sweden with Dane Tom Kristensen.
The 53-year-old Wollek, taking part in his 27th Le Mans, has never won the classic, finising second three times including last year with the same two co-drivers.
